question.prompt: In a mathematics competition, the sum of the scores of Bill and Dick equalled the sum of the scores of Ann and Carol. If the scores of Bill and Carol had been interchanged, then the sum of the scores of Ann and Carol would have exceeded the sum of the scores of the other two. Also, Dick’s score exceeded the sum of the scores of Bill and Carol. Determine the order in which the four contestants finished, from highest to lowest. Assume all scores were nonnegative.

solutions.explanation:
Let \(a,b,c,d\) be the nonnegative scores of Ann, Bill, Carol, and Dick, respectively. The equal totals give
\[
b+d=a+c,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad a-d=b-c.
\]
This connects Ann's advantage over Dick with Bill's advantage over Carol.

After Bill's and Carol's scores are interchanged, Ann and Carol have total \(a+b\), while the other two have total \(d+c\). Thus
\[
a+b>d+c.
\]
Subtracting the right side and using \(a-d=b-c\) gives
\[
0<(a-d)+(b-c)=2(b-c).
\]
Consequently \(b>c\), and the equality of differences also gives \(a>d\).

Finally, Dick's score satisfies \(d>b+c\). Since \(c\ge0\), we have \(d>b+c\ge b\), so \(d>b\). Combining the comparisons yields
\[
a>d>b>c.
\]
The order is therefore \(\boxed{\text{Ann, Dick, Bill, Carol}}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
solutions.title: Compare the score differences
